about.title: Pivot guidance for the Event page
about.written: From public pages, the app's code, and measurements on cases built from public datasets, each listed in sources. A kind's measured field gives counts taken on a case built from the Stolen Szechuan Sauce dataset when the table was written, some of them before the pivot or the parser fix they count was built, so the same case rebuilt with this version can count differently.
about.explained_in: This about block, which describes the table's fields. Each row cites its sources by key in sources.
about.status: The app reads this file for the Event page's next pivots and the counts in To investigate. The reasons, ranks, and default windows are fixed here, each row with its sources, and the app writes none of them.
about.choosing_a_kind: Kinds are tried in order, overlays aside; the first whose match fits the event wins. 'default' matches every event and comes last. An overlay kind (hayabusa_hit) adds its rows after the event's own kind's when its match fits, skipping any pivot the kind already ranks.
about.match: Each key is an events-table column, compared without letter case. A string must equal the column; a list means any of its values; {"contains": s} and {"starts_with": s} test part of the column. {"any_of": [...]} fits when one of its objects fits. has_hayabusa_hit means the event has Hayabusa hits joined (the Event page's ev.hits). Channel and provider names are as Windows writes them. Some come from documentation, not from a case. The same language serves a row's when, a not_offered entry's when, and a caveat's when.
about.pivots: status: built or later. A kind ranks only built pivots; a later pivot appears only in a kind's later list, which the app ignores. A ranked pivot not in pivots.BUILT drops out, with the sentences that send the analyst to it, and the rows below it move up. note names a search that reaches the same events by hand, where there is one.
about.pivot_entry: rank orders the rows. label overrides the pivot's catalog label. args: seconds for window ('case' means the case's time_window_seconds); end for addr (source_ip, dest_ip, remote: the end that isn't one of the seed host's addresses, internal: the end that is a collected host's, external: an end that is not a collected host's address, the first in source, destination order, each: a row per address); value for a file_name row with a fixed name; term for search, with {column} or {data.Field} filled from the event; term_hint where the field name needs checking. when limits a row to events matching it. count false means the row shows no count (a search with a free-text word). breakdown: 'always' for the window row, 'over_limit' for the rest (shown when the count passes 500). broad lists the broad_rules that can flag this row; over_limit applies to every counted row; the window row takes window_text. broad_text replaces the rule's text for this row.
about.caveat: null, or {text, when, check}. text says where the matching misses what the reason promises. when limits it to events that meet the condition. check short_path: once the row is counted, the page shows what the host's MFT says the 8.3 path stands for in the caveat's place, and keeps the caveat where the MFT cannot say.
about.rows_not_in_the_table: A pivot whose key the event lacks moves to the not-offered line with its usual reason (core.js PIVOTS), or with the kind's not_offered reason when its when fits. not_offered_always applies to every kind. A pivot the page offers that a kind doesn't rank goes on one line after the ranked rows, as a plain link with no count, so the page drops none of the pivots it offers.
about.counts: Each counted row's count is an exact case-wide count(*) with the click's own conditions, run after the Event page draws.
about.empty_reasons: The sentences a pivot shows when it finds only the event itself. A sentence with when shows only when its condition fits.

session.label: Same logon session
session.matches: Same host and logon ID, without letter case, with no time bound. A logon ID is unique only until the host restarts, so after a restart the list can join another session's events

account.label: Same account
account.matches: The account key, without letter case: name@realm and user/REALM split, and each spelling of the domain that the case's SIDs show is one domain, with the same name where no domain is recorded

connection.label: Same source IP and port
connection.matches: Same source address and port, within the case's time window around the event. Its list offers the case-wide match, where a reused port joins other connections

addr.label: Same IP at either end
addr.matches: The address as source or destination, as stored

window.label: Same host within ±N s
window.matches: Same host lane within N seconds (1 to 3,600)

search.label: Search
search.matches: A search term the row fills in from the event, which the analyst can also type

file_name.label: Same file name
file_name.matches: The last part of the path (or of the process's, when the event has no path), in any folder, without letter case. A bare name such as SRUM's counts, and so does a capture's URL path

service_name.label: Same service name
service_name.matches: The service's key name or display name, on any host

flow.label: Same flow
flow.matches: Suricata flow_id, or Zeek uid for imported Zeek logs

task_name.label: Same task name
task_name.matches: The task's path and name: TaskName in 4698, 4699, 4702 and Task Scheduler events, Autoruns' Entry for Tasks, RECmd TaskCache's Path

rule.label: Same rule or signature
rule.note: search: code: for a Suricata signature
rule.matches: A Suricata or imported IDS alert's signature (event_code), or a Hayabusa hit's rule title

parent_process.label: Parent process
parent_process.matches: The parent's own creation event: Sysmon ParentProcessGuid, or 4688's creator PID on the same host before this event

hash.label: Same hash
hash.matches: Any of the event's file hashes, lower case, any algorithm: MD5, SHA-1, and SHA-256 from Amcache, Autoruns, Sysmon, Suricata fileinfo, and Zeek files

folder.label: Same folder
folder.matches: Files whose key has the same parent folder

dns_answer.label: DNS answer address
dns_answer.matches: Events at either end of an address the name resolved to

dhcp_lease.label: DHCP lease
dhcp_lease.matches: The lease that held this address at this time

rdp_session.label: Same RDP session
rdp_session.matches: The Remote Desktop session ID on the same host

volume.label: Same volume
volume.matches: The volume serial number a shortcut records

host_at_address.label: Host at this address within ±N s
host_at_address.matches: The lane of the collected host that owns the address, within N seconds

files_loaded.label: Files loaded
files_loaded.matches: Files a Prefetch entry lists as loaded

cache_neighbors.label: Neighboring cache entries
cache_neighbors.matches: AppCompatCache entries next to this one

site.label: Same site
site.matches: The host name of a visited URL, in DNS and capture records

over_limit.test: count > 500 (RELATED_LIMIT), on every counted row; the window row takes window_text, which points to its breakdown by source
over_limit.text: Broad: {count} events. The list shows the 500 nearest in time.
over_limit.window_text: Broad: {count} events. The list shows the 500 nearest in time; open one source from the breakdown to reach the rest.

system_session.test: logon ID is 0x3e7, 0x3e4, 0x3e5, or 0x3e6, without letter case
system_session.text: Broad: this is a system session (SYSTEM, NETWORK SERVICE, LOCAL SERVICE, or ANONYMOUS LOGON). Everything that account does on this host shares it.
system_session.basis: Microsoft names 0x3e7 as LocalSystem's logon ID (LsaGetLogonSessionData). The parser's SYSTEM_SESSIONS comment names 0x3e4 and 0x3e5 as NetworkService's and LocalService's. On Szechuan the Subject of every 0x3e6 event is ANONYMOUS LOGON (101), of 81 of 99 0x3e5 events LOCAL SERVICE, and of 0x3e4 events NETWORK SERVICE or a computer account. No Microsoft page read lists 0x3e4 to 0x3e6 (inference from the samples).

service_account.test: account name is SYSTEM, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, ANONYMOUS LOGON, or matches DWM-<n> or UMFD-<n> (inference: Windows' own window manager and font driver sessions)
service_account.text: Broad: a Windows service account. It acts on every host.

loopback.text: Broad: a loopback address, matched on this host only.

link_local.text: Broad: a link-local address, matched on this host only.

own_address.test: address is one of any collected host's addresses (hosts.ips), whichever event the row starts from, a capture record included
own_address.text: Broad: {host}'s own address. Most of that host's traffic carries it.

system_binary.test: file name is one of svchost.exe, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, conhost.exe, services.exe, winlogon.exe, lsass.exe, explorer.exe, wmiprvse.exe, dllhost.exe, taskhostw.exe
system_binary.text: Broad: a shared Windows program. Every use of it matches.

logon_process.test: Same file on a 4624 or 4625, whose key is the process that handled the logon (ProcessName)
logon_process.text: This is the program that handled the logon, not something the user ran.

weak_time.text: Weak: many entries share this time, so nearby events may be unrelated.

not_offered_always.reason: Logon ID 0x0 is no logon session. A case built by an earlier version of Glessner holds it on 4625s and 4688s until the case is rebuilt.

session.text: No other event shares this logon session.
Process creation and share access are recorded only where their auditing was on.

account.text: No other event names this account in this spelling.

source_ip.text: No other event has this source address.

addr.text: No other event has this address at either end.

connection.text: No other event has this address and port. RDP logons record no port, and NAT changes it.

file.text: No other source names this path. The file may have been deleted before collection, or its MFT, Prefetch, or Amcache wasn't collected.
An 8.3 path such as ADMINI~1 matches the long one only when this host's MFT holds exactly one name it can stand for. Try Same file name for a file whose own name isn't short.

file_name.text: No other file of this name in the case.

window.text: Nothing else on this host in the window. The host's logs may not reach this time: check its earliest event and any log clear (1102, 104).

service_name.text: No other event names this service, by its key name or its display name.

workstation.text: No other event names this client computer. The client supplies the name.

flow.text: No other capture record of this connection.

task_name.text: No other event names this task. Task Scheduler's own log may not have been collected.

rule.text: The rule or signature fired only on this event.

hash.text: No other event has this hash.
Amcache's SHA-1 covers only a file's first 30 MB, so a larger file's entry never matches another source's hash.

kinds.title: 4624 type 3, network logon

pivots.reason: What this logon did here: share access, the admin rights it got (4672), the processes it started, and its logoff.
Where it came from: that machine's other logons and ticket requests, and the capture's records of its traffic.
The capture's records of this connection (SMB, DCE/RPC, or LDAP, and its flow), and other logons made over it.
What followed on this host: a service install (7045), a task, or a process started remotely. In a busy window, open that source from the breakdown.
Where else this account logged on, which shows spread.
Other logons that name the same client computer. The client supplies the name, so treat it as a lead.

pivots.label: Same file (the logon process)
pivots.reason: The program that handled this logon, such as winlogon.exe or services.exe. It shows that program's other events, not what the user did.

kinds.also: The drawn logon link leads to the source host's 4648. With Network Level Authentication, a type 3 can be the first step of an RDP logon (Poling).
kinds.measured: 4624 type 3, DESKTOP to DC01 from port 49752: session 3; account 6,030; source IP 5,869 (Suricata 5,583); either end 6,791. IP and port 4: the other 4624 of the connection 0.3 s later, and a Suricata flow and TLS record 1,079 s later, from another connection on a reused port. Across all 4624 type 3 seeds with a port, the capture's SMB (237 of 364), flow (120 of 202), DCE/RPC (107 of 180), and LDAP (104 of 123) records on the same address and port fall within 5 s once the 3,599.5 s clock offset is applied. Its TLS, DNS, krb5, and HTTP records on them (68) never do.

kinds.title: 4624 type 10, Remote Desktop logon

pivots.reason: What the RDP user did in this session: the processes started, files and shares opened, and the logoff.
The client: its 1149 and RdpCoreTS 131 records, its other logons, and the capture's flows.
What happened in the minutes after the logon. In a busy window, open that source from the breakdown.
Other hosts this account reached by RDP, and failed tries before this one.

pivots.label: Same file (the logon process)
pivots.reason: The program that handled this logon, such as winlogon.exe or services.exe. It shows that program's other events, not what the user did.

not_offered.reason: A type 10 logon records no source port.

later.reason: This session's connect, disconnect, reconnect, and logoff events, by session ID.

kinds.also: Type 10 alone misses the type 3 that Network Level Authentication writes first and the type 7 of a reconnect (Poling). On the client host, look for mstsc.exe and a 4648 to TERMSRV (JPCERT). Reconnects (4778) carry the client's address.
kinds.measured: 4624 type 10 from 194.61.24.102 on DC01: session 4 (4624, 4672, 4634, 4647); account 6,030; source IP 59,286 (Suricata flow 29,313 and TLS 29,207; RdpCoreTS 131 346; 4624 4; 4648 4); either end 59,601; Same file 180 (winlogon.exe). Window ±300 s: 64,178, of them Schannel 36888 and 36874 29,205 each. The 500 nearest reach 8.7 s (median over 5 type 10 seeds).

kinds.title: 4625, failed logon

pivots.reason: Is one address trying many accounts or passwords? Look for a 4624 from it after the failures.
Failures and successes from the same client name. Use it when the address is empty.
Is one account failing from many places, or on many hosts?
Did a successful logon follow the failures? In a busy window, open that source from the breakdown.

pivots.label: Same failure reason
pivots.reason: Same failure reason: 0xC0000064 means the user name doesn't exist, 0xC000006A a wrong password.

not_offered.reason: A 4625's logon ID belongs to the process that reported it (0x0, or SYSTEM's 0x3e7), not to a logon session.

kinds.also: No 4625 doesn't mean no guessing: lockout changes what is logged, and network failures may appear only on the target (Valhuntir).
kinds.measured: 4625 type 3 with no address, workstation kali: account 0 (no domain); window ±60 s 1,990; Same workstation 99, which is 95 failures and 4 successes.

kinds.title: 4776, NTLM credential validation

pivots.reason: Where else this account authenticated. On a domain controller this is every NTLM validation of a domain account.
Validations and logons from the same client computer.
The logon this validation served, and failures around it (Error Code not 0x0).

kinds.also: 4776 is written only on the computer that holds the account: the domain controller for a domain account, the host itself for a local one. It names the client but not the server the user reached (Microsoft, 4776).
kinds.measured: 12 events; account set on all 12, domain on none, workstation on none.

kinds.title: 4648, logon with explicit credentials

pivots.reason: What the person who supplied the credentials was doing in that logon.

pivots.label: Same file (the process)
pivots.reason: Which program used the credentials: runas, schtasks, mstsc, net, or a tool.
Where else these credentials were used.
The commands around it on this host.

kinds.also: The drawn logon link leads to the target server the event names; the 4624 there shows whether the logon worked. Scheduled tasks, RunAs, and mapped drives write 4648 too.
kinds.measured: 4648 with SubjectLogonId 0x3E7: session 1,110 (4907 641, 4624 type 5 154, 4672 154); account 35; source IP 62 (127.0.0.1); Same file 180; window ±60 s 7,561.

kinds.title: 4672, special privileges assigned

pivots.reason: Which logon got admin rights. Pair it with its 4624 and see what that session did.
Is this account expected to hold admin rights on this host?
What the privileged session did straight away.

kinds.also: Every SYSTEM logon writes a 4672, so it doesn't show escalation by itself.
kinds.measured: 4672 for Administrator: session 3; account 6,030; window ±60 s 1,502.

kinds.title: 4768, 4769, 4771, Kerberos ticket requests

pivots.reason: The client machine: its other ticket requests and logons.
The capture's krb5 and flow records of this request.
This account's other activity.
Logons and ticket requests around it.

kinds.also: A ticket request and the network logon it leads to are separate connections, so they don't share a source port (inference from the protocols: Kerberos goes to the KDC on port 88). On Szechuan none of 89 Kerberos events with a port shares it with a 4624 within 5 s; the 19 that share it at all are at least 1,014 s apart.
kinds.measured: 4769 for Administrator@C137.LOCAL: account 28 (4769s only); source IP 5,869; IP and port 3: the 4769, then a flow and a TLS record 1,079 s later on a reused port; either end 6,791; window ±60 s 197. Across Kerberos seeds, the capture's krb5 (28 of 42) and flow (28 of 73) records sharing the address and port fall within 5 s once the clock offset is applied; DCE/RPC, TLS, LDAP, HTTP, and DNS records (59) never do.

kinds.also: The sources disagree on 1149: JPCERT reads it as authentication succeeded, Poling as a network connection made before credentials are entered.
kinds.measured: RemoteConnectionManager 261: no pivot field filled; window ±60 s 61,778 during the brute force (Schannel 36888 and 36874, 29,205 each).

kinds.title: 4688 and Sysmon 1, process created

pivots.reason: Which logon ran it. Follow it to the 4624 and that logon's source.

pivots.label: Same file (the program)
pivots.reason: When the program landed (MFT, USN), and whether it ran before (Prefetch, Amcache).

kinds.title: 7045 and 4697, service installed

pivots.label: Same file (the service binary)
pivots.reason: Did the binary land (MFT, USN, a write to ADMIN$), and did it run (Prefetch, process creation)?
pivots.broad_text: Broad when the path is svchost.exe -k: every shared service matches.

caveat.text: An 8.3 path such as ADMINI~1 matches the long one only when this host's MFT holds exactly one name it can stand for.

pivots.reason: The logon that installed it (4624 type 3 with a 4672) and the share access just before. In a busy window, open that source from the breakdown.
The same service on other hosts shows spread. State changes on this host show it started, when they were logged.

pivots.label: Same account (from the System element)
pivots.reason: The account the event's System element names. In the EVTX-ATTACK-SAMPLES events checked, that was the remote installer; beyond them it is inference. A service SYSTEM installed has none.
Who installed it, and from which logon.
The binary's name on other hosts or in other folders, as with PsExec's PSEXESVC.exe.

not_offered.reason: A 7045 records no logon ID.
A service install records no address.

kinds.also: A later change to the service's path or account goes unlogged (Microsoft, 4697). PsExec can rename its service with -r (Valhuntir). The sources differ on which record to use: ATT&CK's DET0552 lists 4697, JPCERT and Valhuntir use 7045. The 7045 caveat in caveats.json says the account shown is the one the System element names, which was the installer in the EVTX-ATTACK-SAMPLES events checked.
kinds.measured: 7045 coreupdater on DC01: Same file 30 (MFT 11, USN 10, SRUM 3, 7045 2, Autoruns 2, Amcache 1, Prefetch 1; 19 of them on DESKTOP); Same file name 49, or 53 with bare names; account 6,030. Same service name 6 with RECmd's Services rows (the 7045, Autoruns, and RECmd on each host), 4 without. Window ±600 s: 65,001, of them Schannel 36888 and 36874 29,205 each; the nearest event log records are the installing 4624 type 3 and 4672, at 0.0 s. Across 40 7045 seeds the 500 nearest reach a median 0.92 s, and 4 of 40 lists hold a 4624 before the install. 7045 for the vmmemctl driver: Same file 13; service name by the written name 2, missing Autoruns' VMMemCtl; window ±60 s 3,546.
